content.value_statement: Teams often ship code with tests added too late to prove behavior. This skill guides a strict red-green-refactor workflow with failure checks, minimal implementation, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Prompts users to write a failing test before implementation.
Defines red, green, and refactor steps for feature work.
Provides examples of good and poor tests in TypeScript.
Lists verification checks before marking work complete.
References testing anti-patterns for mocks and test utilities.
limitations: Does not run tests or inspect project results by itself.
Requires a project with an existing test framework.
Uses TypeScript examples, though the workflow is language independent.
May be too strict for disposable prototypes unless a human approves an exception.

use_cases.title: Add a Feature Test First
use_cases.description: Plan the first failing test, implement the smallest behavior, and verify the feature through focused tests.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression With Proof
use_cases.description: Create a failing regression test before changing code, then confirm the bug cannot return silently.

use_cases.title: Review Testing Discipline
use_cases.description: Check whether a change followed red-green-refactor and avoided weak mocks or test-after habits.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through TDD for this feature: [describe feature]. Start by proposing one failing test and expected failure.

prompt_templates.title: Write the Red Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write the smallest failing test for this behavior: [behavior]. Include what failure I should see before coding.

prompt_templates.title: Go Green Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: My failing test is ready for [behavior]. Suggest the minimal implementation and the checks needed before refactoring.

prompt_templates.title: Audit TDD Discipline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tested change for TDD discipline: [summary]. Identify missing failure proof, over-mocking, or over-engineering before completion.

output_examples.input: I need to add retry behavior to a failing operation.
output: Write one focused test for retrying a failed operation.
Run the focused test and confirm it fails because retry is missing.
Implement only the retry behavior needed to pass that test.
Run related tests before refactoring names or helpers.

output_examples.input: A bug accepts empty email addresses.
output_examples.output: Create a failing regression test that expects empty email input to be rejected. Then add the smallest validation change and rerun the test.

output_examples.input: My test uses a large mock setup.
output: Check whether the test asserts behavior or mock details.
Mock only the slow or external boundary that the test does not need.

best_practices: Run each new test once before implementation and record the expected failure.
Implement only enough behavior to make the current failing test pass.
Refactor only after the focused test and related tests are green.
anti_patterns: Writing production code before a failing test exists.
Keeping exploratory code as a reference while writing tests.
Asserting on mock details instead of user-visible behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests for me?
faq.answer: It guides test design and implementation order. You still adapt tests to your project and framework.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it run my test suite?
faq.answer: No. It tells you when to run focused tests and what to verify.

faq.question: Is it language-specific?
faq.answer: No. Examples use TypeScript, but the TDD process applies to many languages.

faq.question: What if I already wrote implementation code?
faq.answer: The skill recommends deleting or setting aside that code, then starting from a failing test.

faq.question: When should I skip TDD?
faq.answer: Only for approved exceptions such as throwaway prototypes, generated code, or configuration changes.
